President Trump says White House Chief of Staff Suzy Wiles is being replaced by Steven
Miller, who's currently the Deputy Chief of Staff.
Miller is Trump's closest advisor and the architect of his hardline immigration policy.
It's a major shake-up, just days after the Republicans' historic losses in the midterm
elections and a sign that the White House isn't backing down from its agenda.

Wiles was known to be a savvy political operator.

Trump's desires.
He was an aide to Alabama Senator Jeff Sessions, who became Trump's first attorney general.

to expand Trump's power.
And Piers Daniel Kurtzleben reporting.
One of the major takeaways from the 2024 election was the Democrats lost ground with young voters
who shifted right toward Donald Trump.
But this week, voters under the age of 30 issued a strong rebuke of the president and
his party, voting decisively for Democrats.
And Piers Elena Moore reports.
In recent elections, Democrats have done well when they win young voters by a margin of
at least 20 points.
On Tuesday, they carried the group by nearly 50 points, according to exit polls.
It's the largest margin Democrats have had with young people in decades.
And though young voters do turn out at lower rates than older voters, that sizable support
made a difference on the margins.
An example, the Texas Senate race.

Looking at just Gen Z, though, voters under 30, he won it by 60 points.
Elena Moore, NPR News, Washington.
Google, Meta and TikTok are suing California to block a new law aimed at shielding kids
from addictive social media features like personalized feeds and autoplay for videos.
Rachel Miro of member station KQED has more.
In separate lawsuits, Google, Meta and TikTok argue the new law, which takes effect in January,
violates their free speech rights and wrongly substitutes the state's judgment for that
of parents.
Rin Alajaji is with the digital rights group, the Electronic Frontier Foundation, which
opposed the bill.
It's a functional ban for young people under 16.
It cuts young people off from essential information and experiences online.
It silences the very voices it plans to protect.
The California Attorney General's office says it's reviewing the lawsuits, adding, quote,
our office is committed to defending California's common sense laws to protect kids online.
For NPR News, I'm Rachel Miro.
You're listening to NPR News from Washington.
Voters are going to the polls in New Zealand to cast their ballots in the country's general
election.
High inflation and housing affordability are some of the key issues, as Adam Hancock reports.
Economic issues are set to be front of mind for voters.
New Zealand is facing a cost of living crisis with inflation at 3.7 percent and unemployment
at its highest level since 2015.
There are also concerns about the availability and affordability of housing, although property
prices are now 17 percent below their peak in early 2022.
Polls will close at 7 p.m. local time, with preliminary results expected a few hours later.
Left-leaning parties, including Labour, are looking to make the incumbent coalition led
by the Centerite National Party the first one-term government in nearly 50 years.
Official results, including overseas ballots, will be declared on November the 27th.
For NPR News, I'm Adam Hancock in Sydney.

Jobs were created in professional and business services, health care and manufacturing.
Wall Street ended the day in mixed territory.
The Dow was down 237 points, the Nasdaq up 264.
I'm Janine Herbst, NPR News, in Washington.
